checks: Positive sampled endpoint masses are finite and full-dimensional, so the ordinary marked depth theorem applies for d≥2. In d=1 the positive support is an interval and its absolutely continuous law has an interior median with both tails of mass one half. Joint log-concavity makes every interpolated marked value positive.

The affine ambient margin along the marks makes the captured indices a prefix, suffix or full chain containing i. In each captured fiber the cap trace contains its parallel continuous halfspace through that interpolated mark.

After truncating the two endpoint densities to their through-mark continuous caps, interpolation of any two retained points stays in the corresponding intermediate truncation by linearity of its margin. Joint log-concavity then gives exactly the Prékopa–Leindler hypothesis at the interpolation weight. If either endpoint value is zero, the pointwise inequality follows from nonnegativity.

Prékopa–Leindler gives Γ_d a^(1−j/L)b^(j/L) for every intermediate captured fiber. At the endpoints the marked depth bound gives the same statement, and for a pure-base cap use the full fiber densities with a whole trace. Distinct integer sites add disjoint mass, and the normalization retains every original sampled fiber in M.

For L=2 the smaller inclusive tail is √(ab)+min(a,b). In the equal-endpoint three-site case, if the middle mass m is at least 2a its own mark pays at least Γ_d M/2, and otherwise the midpoint sum 2a does so.

dependencies.hypotheses: Apply its attained ordinary depth lower bound to each positive endpoint fiber (and to the middle fiber in the heavy case) in dimension d≥2. The extended inverse power is convex as an increasing convex exponential of −log f divided by any β>d+1. Boundary modification for its representative is on a Lebesgue-null set and leaves cap masses unchanged. The attaining mark is in the positive interior, so the original joint density is positive there.

overlap.comparison: The equal-endpoint consequence is already true for three uniform compatible convex fibers, by a different two-cut theorem. It does not give the marked geometric-tail formula for joint log-concave densities.
The accepted equal-volume compact convex-family conclusion selects a true uniform fiber centroid, without a chordwise bound or varying sampled densities.
